<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make `EngineCore` and its workers exit, and release the GPUs, when the process that launched them dies without shutting them down (SIGKILL, OOM-kill, crash). Fixes #55510. Same class of report as #19849, #25850, #34643 and #43060.

## Claims

- When the launching process is SIGKILLed, `VLLM::EngineCore` and its `VLLM::Worker_TP*` processes exit within 15 s and release GPU memory. On `main` they keep running indefinitely, and a restart then fails the KV-cache memory check or OOMs.
- Validated for `vllm serve` TP=2, `vllm serve` DP=2, offline `LLM()` with TP=1/2, and SIGKILL during model loading. @vinitrbl independently confirmed `vllm run-batch` ([review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55846#pullrequestreview-5424839487)): on `main` even a plain SIGTERM orphans the engine there, because run-batch has no SIGTERM handler, and with this PR the GPU is free within 5 s for both SIGTERM and SIGKILL.
- Clients that outlive the dead parent receive `ENGINE_CORE_DEAD` and fail fast instead of hanging with `/health` 200. The main example is the API-server processes in multi-API-server mode, which is the default for DP > 1.
- Nothing changes while the parent is alive. SIGTERM/SIGINT handling and the `--shutdown-timeout` drain path are untouched, and the existing shutdown tests listed below pass.

## Validation

Base `84bcbc6264`, torch 2.13.0+cu132. The branch has since been rebased onto `04462732a4` with no conflicts and an unchanged patch. The reproducer and the existing shutdown suites ran on 2× A100-SXM4-40GB (driver 580.159.03). The final test files ran on 2× A100-PCIE-40GB (driver 595.71.05) with `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK=0`. That host needs them for TP=2 because its GPUs sit on different sockets and P2P does not work inside its container. NVIDIA only: ROCm was not validated, but the AMD "Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown" mirror runs the new test.

Reproducer for #55510: start `vllm serve hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --enforce-eager`, `kill -9` the launcher, then watch `ps` and `nvidia-smi`.

| Scenario | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP=2, SIGKILL the API server | EngineCore + 2 workers still alive after 60 s, 75,856 MiB held | all exited after 8 s, 0 MiB |
| DP=2 (2 API servers), SIGKILL the launcher | 2 EngineCores + 2 workers still alive after 60 s, 75,240 MiB held; the API servers keep serving | engines exited after 7 s, 0 MiB; both API servers got `EngineDeadError` and shut down on their own ~4 s later (only the CPU-only DP coordinator remains) |
| TP=2, SIGKILL during model load | EngineCore finishes loading, starts its workers and holds 75,856 MiB after 60 s | all exited within 1 s, 0 MiB |

In every PR run the engine log shows `parent process exited, shutting down` followed by the normal abort and teardown; the 15 s force-kill fallback never fired.

```
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py                       # 19 passed
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 pytest -v -s tests/v1/shutdown/test_parent_death.py # 2 passed (TP=1: 33 s, TP=2: 53 s)
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 pytest -v -s tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py tests/v1/shutdown/test_forward_error.py tests/v1/shutdown/test_startup_error.py  # 18 passed, 4 skipped
pytest -v -s tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_shutdown.py                    # 8 passed (SIGTERM drain/abort unchanged)
```

On unpatched `main`, `test_parent_death.py` fails in both cases with `engine processes outlived their parent`. For TP=2 the survivors are EngineCore and both TP workers. `pre-commit` (ruff, typos) and mypy (`--python-version 3.12`) pass.

## Details

**Root cause.** `WorkerProc` already exits when its parent dies: `MultiprocExecutor` gives each worker the read end of a death pipe and keeps the write end. But the workers' parent is `EngineCore`, and `EngineCore` has no parent-liveness check of its own:
- `CoreEngineProcManager` starts it as a plain non-daemon process.
- `run_engine_core` installs only SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers.
- Its ZMQ sockets have no heartbeat.

So when the frontend disappears, `EngineCore` idles forever and keeps its workers alive.

**Fix.** Reuse the worker mechanism one level up.
- **Shared helper.** The worker's death-pipe thread moves without behaviour changes into `vllm.utils.system_utils.monitor_parent_death()`, and `WorkerProc` calls it.
- **Pipe ownership.** `CoreEngineProcManager` creates one pipe per engine and holds the write ends until after `shutdown(procs)` has stopped the engines, so a SIGTERM drain never sees EOF. Under fork, children close the inherited write ends, as `MultiprocExecutor` already does.
- **On EOF.** `EngineCore` follows the approach @njhill suggested on #34816: "set the shutdown flag and then kill after some delay".
  - It sends `ENGINE_CORE_DEAD` to its clients.
  - It requests shutdown in abort mode and wakes the busy loop, so the normal teardown runs and terminates the workers.
  - If it is still alive 15 s later, or if the parent died before the engine finished initializing, it SIGKILLs its process tree and then itself.

<details>
<summary>Design notes and alternatives</summary>

- **Abort, not drain.** A drain is only ever bounded by the parent force-killing the engine when `--shutdown-timeout` expires, so without the parent a drain would be unbounded. RFC #24885 puts that decision with the parent, and that parent is gone. `--shutdown-timeout` defaults to 0, so default deployments abort anyway.
- **Notify clients at EOF time.** The notice goes out before teardown rather than after it, so it cannot be pre-empted by the 15 s force-kill and does not delay GPU release. As a result, in-flight requests on surviving clients fail with `EngineDeadError`, the same as when an engine crashes.
- **Not `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG)`** (#34816, draft #40935).
  - The death pipe is portable and pure Python; on #40841 prctl was described as "not easy to do in python".
  - It tracks the parent *process* rather than the thread that created the child, which matters for embedders that construct `LLM()` from a helper thread.
  - It allows a cooperative abort before any kill.
- **Not `multiprocessing.parent_process().sentinel`.** Under fork, CPython's parent keeps each child's sentinel write end open, so later siblings inherit the write ends of earlier siblings and EOF would cascade one engine at a time.
- **Earlier attempts.** #27686, #36055 and #34816 were closed for inactivity, not rejected. Compared with them, this PR keeps the `processes` API, handles inherited fds under fork, closes the write ends only after the engines have shut down (so drain is preserved), and installs no new signal handlers.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Not covered, and behaviour changes</summary>

Not covered:
- The DP supervisor itself being SIGKILLed. Its DP servers run in their own process group and keep their engines. Death of a single DP server *is* covered.
- `vllm-rs serve` managed-engine mode when the Rust binary dies, because the headless Python launcher survives it.
- CPU-only processes left behind by a SIGKILLed multi-API-server launcher: API servers (which now see `EngineDeadError`), the DP coordinator and the Rust frontend. Related: #43417.
- Ray-managed engines.
- If user code forks after creating `LLM()`, for example with a fork-mode `multiprocessing.Pool`, those children hold the write end and delay EOF until they exit. The existing worker death pipe has the same limitation.
- A narrow startup race. If the parent dies while EngineCore is still starting its TP workers, the force-kill takes a single process-tree snapshot, so a worker started in the few milliseconds after it can be missed. That worker only exits at the distributed-init timeout (600 s by default), because workers start watching their death pipe after `WorkerProc` construction. This gap already exists on `main`, for example when EngineCore is OOM-killed while spawning workers. Closing it on the worker side is left for a follow-up.

Behaviour changes:
- If the parent dies during a SIGTERM drain, the engine switches to abort.
- Multi-node DP: when one node's launcher dies, that node's ranks now exit instead of being left orphaned. They notify the head node and are force-killed after 15 s if their peers are still busy, so the DP group fails the same way it does when any rank dies.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Interaction with open PRs</summary>

- #52299 (merged since) is complementary: it handles SIGTERM during init, while this PR handles parent death during init. #50529 applies cleanly on top of this PR.
- #55700 needs a one-line move: its `dump_stack` call goes into the new `on_parent_death` closure in `WorkerProc.monitor_death_pipe`.
- The `kill_process_tree` regression from #52314, where it can raise `psutil.NoSuchProcess`, is fixed separately in #59984. The force-kill here performs its final self-SIGKILL either way.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the patch, the tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU experiments above.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Gave this a try with `vllm run-batch`, since it isn't in the table and it's a slightly worse case: run-batch has no SIGTERM handler, so even a normal SIGTERM kills the launcher without telling the engine.

A10G, tiny random-weight Llama, 4000-request batch, signal sent to the run-batch process once a few hundred requests had finished. Base is main at the merge base (7867d6c), PR head 81aa514, both with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

| signal | main @ 7867d6c | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| SIGTERM | EngineCore still up after 60s, 21 GB held | gone, GPU free within 5s |
| SIGKILL | | gone, GPU free within 5s |

Both PR runs log `EngineCore: parent process exited, shutting down`. I didn't redo SIGKILL on 7867d6c, but on another main-based build (the #52505 branch) it orphaned the engine the same way.

On main the next run on the same GPU fails in `request_memory` until you kill the orphan by hand, so this is a nice fix for anyone retrying interrupted batch jobs. Might be worth adding run-batch to the list of covered cases.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Test that EngineCore and its workers exit when their parent process dies
+without shutting them down (API server SIGKILLed, OOM-killed or crashed)."""
+
+import contextlib
+import multiprocessing
+import os
+import signal
+import time
+
+import psutil
+import pytest
+
+from tests.utils import wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear
+from tests.v1.shutdown.utils import (
+    SHUTDOWN_TEST_THRESHOLD_BYTES,
+    SHUTDOWN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.engine.core import PARENT_DEATH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S
+
+MODELS = ["hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"]
+
+# Cooperative shutdown budget plus a margin for the force-kill fallback.
+ORPHAN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SEC = PARENT_DEATH_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S + 30
+
+
+def _serve_until_killed(model: str, tensor_parallel_size: int, conn) -> None:
+    """Child process: start an LLM, report its engine process tree, then idle
+    until the test kills this process."""
+    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+
+    llm = LLM(
+        model=model,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        tensor_parallel_size=tensor_parallel_size,
+    )
+    llm.generate("Hello my name is", SamplingParams(max_tokens=1))
+    conn.send([child.pid for child in psutil.Process().children(recursive=True)])
+    conn.close()
+    while True:
+        time.sleep(1)
+
+
+def _is_running(pid: int) -> bool:
+    try:
+        return psutil.Process(pid).status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE
+    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
+        return False
+
+
+def _wait_until_gone(pids: list[int], timeout: float) -> list[int]:
+    """Return the pids still running after ``timeout`` seconds."""
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while True:
+        alive = [pid for pid in pids if _is_running(pid)]
+        if not alive or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+            return alive
+        time.sleep(0.5)
+
+
+def _kill_all(pids: list[int]) -> None:
+    for pid in pids:
+        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
+            os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.timeout(SHUTDOWN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC * 2)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model", MODELS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tensor_parallel_size", [2, 1])
+def test_engine_exits_after_parent_sigkill(model: str, tensor_parallel_size: int):
+    """SIGKILL the process that owns a running LLM; EngineCore and every
+    worker must exit on their own and release GPU memory."""
+    if current_platform.device_count() < tensor_parallel_size:
+        pytest.skip(reason="Not enough CUDA devices")
+
+    ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
+    parent_conn, child_conn = ctx.Pipe(duplex=False)
+    proc = ctx.Process(
+        target=_serve_until_killed, args=(model, tensor_parallel_size, child_conn)
+    )
+    proc.start()
+    child_conn.close()
+    assert proc.pid is not None
+    parent_pid = proc.pid
+    engine_pids: list[int] = []
+    try:
+        assert parent_conn.poll(SHUTDOWN_TEST_TIMEOUT_SEC), "LLM did not start"
+        engine_pids = parent_conn.recv()
+        # EngineCore, plus one worker per rank when TP > 1.
+        expected = 1 + (tensor_parallel_size if tensor_parallel_size > 1 else 0)
+        assert len(engine_pids) >= expected, engine_pids
+        assert all(_is_running(pid) for pid in engine_pids)
+
+        os.kill(parent_pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        proc.join(10)
+        assert proc.exitcode == -signal.SIGKILL
+
+        orphans = _wait_until_gone(engine_pids, ORPHAN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_SEC)
+        assert not orphans, f"engine processes outlived their parent: {orphans}"
+    finally:
+        if proc.is_alive():
+            proc.kill()
+        _kill_all(engine_pids)
+
+    wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear(
+        devices=list(range(tensor_parallel_size)),
+        threshold_bytes=SHUTDOWN_TEST_THRESHOLD_BYTES,
+    )

 import sys

 from collections.abc import Callable, Iterator

 from pathlib import Path
 
 import psutil
@@ -234,6 +236,34 @@ def kill_process_tree(pid: int):
         os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
 
 
+def monitor_parent_death(
+    death_pipe: Connection | None,
+    on_parent_death: Callable[[], None],
+    *,
+    name: str = "DeathPipeMonitor",
+) -> None:
+    """Run ``on_parent_death`` on a daemon thread once ``death_pipe`` hits EOF.
+
+    The parent keeps the write end open and never writes to it; the kernel
+    closes it when the parent exits by any means, including SIGKILL. Children
+    started with fork must close every inherited copy of the write end,
+    including their own.
+    """
+    if death_pipe is None:

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Gave this a try with `vllm run-batch`, since it isn't in the table and it's a slightly worse case: run-batch has no SIGTERM handler, so even a normal SIGTERM kills the launcher without telling the engine.

A10G, tiny random-weight Llama, 4000-request batch, signal sent to the run-batch process once a few hundred requests had finished. Base is main at the merge base (7867d6c), PR head 81aa514, both with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

| signal | main @ 7867d6c | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| SIGTERM | EngineCore still up after 60s, 21 GB held | gone, GPU free within 5s |
| SIGKILL | | gone, GPU free within 5s |

Both PR runs log `EngineCore: parent process exited, shutting down`. I didn't redo SIGKILL on 7867d6c, but on another main-based build (the #52505 branch) it orphaned the engine the same way.

On main the next run on the same GPU fails in `request_memory` until you kill the orphan by hand, so this is a nice fix for anyone retrying interrupted batch jobs. Might be worth adding run-batch to the list of covered cases.
